amendments.body: In `nitrogen_cycle.rs` lines 131-134, the `.max(0.0)` clamps on `(don_consumed_mg - live_biomass_nitrogen_mg(decomp_growth, n_to_c)).max(0.0)` and the equivalent carbon line silently swallow tiny negative values from floating-point rounding in `constrained_live_growth_g`. While the constraint function prevents meaningful overruns, repeated rounding over long simulations could accumulate a drift that the 1e-6 guard tolerance masks. Consider asserting via `debug_assert!` that the pre-clamp value is >= some small negative threshold (e.g., -1e-9) so that a logic error in `constrained_live_growth_g` doesn't silently leak mass.
amendments.rationale: The `.max(0.0)` clamp is a valid floating-point safety measure, but it also masks potential bugs. If `constrained_live_growth_g` is ever changed to be less conservative, the clamp would silently absorb real nitrogen/carbon leaks. A debug_assert guards against this while keeping the runtime clamp.

amendments.body: The `test_budget_component_labels_cover_all_element_bearing_fields` structural coverage test relies on naming conventions (`*_mg_n_total`, `*_mg_c_total`, `*biomass_g`, etc.) to auto-discover budget-relevant fields. If a future pool uses a non-standard name (e.g., `organic_sludge_mg` instead of `organic_sludge_g_total`), it will silently escape the coverage check. The doc-comments on `nitrogen_budget_components` and `carbon_budget_components` mention this risk but provide no compile-time or CI enforcement. Consider adding a `#[deny(unused)]` marker attribute or a manual registry pattern that forces new TankState fields to explicitly opt in or out of budget tracking.
amendments.rationale: The structural coverage test is the primary safety net ensuring new pools aren't missed. Its effectiveness depends entirely on naming conventions being followed. A single non-conforming field name would create an invisible conservation hole, which is the exact class of bug this infrastructure exists to prevent.

amendments.body: The `SiphonDetritus` action is classified as open-system in `is_open_system_action_label` but has no dedicated budget tracking test verifying that the exported mass is properly recorded as an explicit export in the ledger (unlike `WaterChangePercent` which has `test_water_change_n_export_tracked`). Add a test analogous to `test_water_change_n_export_tracked` that siphons detritus, verifies total N/C decreased by the expected amount, and confirms the budget ledger entry shows the export as an explicit outflow rather than unexplained loss.
amendments.rationale: The acceptance criteria explicitly require that open-system operations show as explicit exports. Water change has this test, but siphon detritus (which also exports mass) does not. The guard would pass silently even if siphon tracking were broken because the open-system classification exempts it from the guard check.

payload.summary: The per-tick mass budget tracking implementation is well-designed and correct. Key strengths: (1) canonical `total_nitrogen_mg`/`total_carbon_mg` helpers defined once in `budget.rs` with fixed-size array components that enforce compile-time completeness, (2) structural coverage test using JSON reflection to auto-detect new element-bearing fields, (3) runtime budget guard (`enforce_tracked_tick_budget_guard`) that returns `SimError::BudgetImbalance` when tracking is enabled, with proper separation of open-system actions and chemistry DIC exchange, (4) truly zero-cost when disabled (Option-based gating, no allocations). All 18 budget tracking tests pass on the committed state. Conservation correctness was verified across all major pathways: nitrification, decomposer mineralization, plant/algae growth and decay, shrimp feeding/mortality/reproduction, water changes, trim plants, clean filter. The chemistry test failures (`solver_edge_case_zero_dic`, `solver_edge_case_zero_alkalinity`) are caused by unrelated unstaged WIP changes, not by budget tracking code. Three minor amendments proposed around defensive assertions, naming-convention fragility in structural coverage, and missing test coverage for SiphonDetritus open-system export tracking.
